## Loading

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| error: false

library(tidyverse)
library(easystats)
library(brms)
library(rstan)
library(patchwork)
library(ggside)
library(ggdist)

restore_units <- function(df, illusion = NULL) {
  if(!is.null(illusion)) df$Illusion_Type <- illusion
  df <- df |> 
    mutate(
      # Inverse of fit_model.R's normalisation. Difference is on [-1, 1] with 0
      # at the per-illusion mid-point difficulty (2026-09-20); a fit made before
      # that is on [0, 1] and cannot be read with this function. The bounds are
      # the observed per-illusion min/max of abs(Illusion_Difference) -- the
      # Ebbinghaus min (0.05, not 0.07) and the VerticalHorizontal max (0.30,
      # not 0.24) were wrong until 2026-09-20.
      Illusion_Difference = case_when(
        Illusion_Type == "MullerLyer" ~ (Illusion_DifferenceZ + 1) / 2 * (0.46 - 0.04) + 0.04,
        Illusion_Type == "Ebbinghaus" ~ (Illusion_DifferenceZ + 1) / 2 * (0.70 - 0.05) + 0.05,
        Illusion_Type == "VerticalHorizontal" ~ (Illusion_DifferenceZ + 1) / 2 * (0.30 - 0.03) + 0.03,
        .default = NA
      ),
      Illusion_Strength = case_when(
        Illusion_Type == "MullerLyer" ~ Illusion_StrengthZ * 49,
        Illusion_Type == "Ebbinghaus" ~ Illusion_StrengthZ * 2.03,
        Illusion_Type == "VerticalHorizontal" ~ Illusion_StrengthZ * 66.50,
        .default = NA
      )
  )
}

# Inverse of restore_units(): raw units -> the Z scale the models were fitted
# on, e.g. to build a prediction grid over a custom range. The bounds must match
# those of restore_units(). A lookup by name rather than case_when(), which no
# longer accepts a single `type` against a vector `x` (deprecated in dplyr
# 1.2.0); this way `type` can be one illusion or one per value of `x`, and an
# unknown illusion gives NA.
normalize_units <- function(x, type = "MullerLyer", what = "Strength") {
  what <- match.arg(what, c("Strength", "Difference"))
  if (what == "Strength") {
    scale <- c(MullerLyer = 49, Ebbinghaus = 2.03, VerticalHorizontal = 66.50)[type]
    unname(x / scale)
  } else {
    # The models only see the size of the difference, not its side
    # (fit_model.R takes abs() before normalising), so neither does this
    x <- abs(x)
    lo <- c(MullerLyer = 0.04, Ebbinghaus = 0.05, VerticalHorizontal = 0.03)[type]
    hi <- c(MullerLyer = 0.46, Ebbinghaus = 0.70, VerticalHorizontal = 0.30)[type]
    unname((x - lo) / (hi - lo) * 2 - 1)
  }
}
```

#| warning: false

# path <- "C:/Users/olive/Documents/"
path <- "C:/Users/domma/Dropbox/RECHERCHE/Studies/IllusionGameComputational/analysis/models/"

# A fit does not know which illusion it was fitted to: its data only has the
# Z-scored predictors, and combine_model.R drops $file. The file name is the one
# place it is recorded (<model>_<illusion>[_suffix].rds), so it is attached to
# the fit here, for model_illusion() below.
load_fit <- function(file) {
  illusion <- regmatches(file, regexpr("MullerLyer|Ebbinghaus|VerticalHorizontal", file))
  if (length(illusion) == 0) stop("No illusion in the file name: ", file)
  m <- readRDS(paste0(path, file))
  attr(m, "illusion") <- illusion
  m
}
gam_lnr_muller <- load_fit("gam_lnr_MullerLyer.rds")
gam_lnr6_muller <- load_fit("gam_lnr6_MullerLyer.rds")
gam_ddm4_muller <- load_fit("gam_ddm4_MullerLyer.rds")

# The models to compare, in the order they should appear in the plots below.
# Everything downstream loops over this list, so adding a model here is the only
# change needed to get it into the predictive check, the curves and the heatmaps.
models <- list(
  "LNR" = gam_lnr_muller,
  "LNR-6" = gam_lnr6_muller,
  "DDM-4" = gam_ddm4_muller
)

## Computational Cost

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

# Sampling efficiency: bulk effective sample size per hour of sampling wall
# clock, computed chain by chain so that the spread across chains is visible.
# Only the population-level parameters are counted (the smooth coefficients,
# their SDs and the group-level SDs): the thousands of participant offsets would
# otherwise dominate the average and say more about the data than the sampler.
data_efficiency <- function(m, pars = "^b_|^bs_|^sd_|^sds_") {
  draws <- posterior::as_draws_array(m, variable = pars, regex = TRUE)
  # Time per chain. Efficiency is per hour of *sampling*, the usual
  # convention, but what one actually waits for is warmup + sampling, so both
  # are kept. This is wall clock, so it is only comparable between fits of the
  # same data with the same number of threads per chain - hence those are
  # carried along too and printed under the plot.
  time <- rstan::get_elapsed_time(m$fit)
  threads <- as.numeric(m$fit@stan_args[[1]]$num_threads)

  purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(posterior::nchains(draws)), function(chain) {
    # Parameters that were fixed rather than estimated (sigmadrift = 0 and the
    # like) have no effective sample size, hence the na.rm
    ess <- posterior::summarise_draws(
      posterior::subset_draws(draws, chain = chain),
      ess_bulk = posterior::ess_bulk
    )$ess_bulk
    data.frame(
      Chain = chain,
      ESS = mean(ess, na.rm = TRUE),
      Time_warmup = time[[chain, "warmup"]],
      Time_sample = time[[chain, "sample"]],
      Time_total = time[[chain, "warmup"]] + time[[chain, "sample"]],
      # get_elapsed_time() is in seconds
      ESS_per_hour = mean(ess, na.rm = TRUE) / (time[[chain, "sample"]] / 3600),
      Threads = if (length(threads) == 1) threads else NA_real_,
      N = stats::nobs(m)
    )
  })
}

efficiency <- purrr::imap_dfr(models, \(m, name) mutate(data_efficiency(m), Model = name)) |>
  mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = names(models)))

# Model-level summary: the chains of a model average to one point
efficiency_means <- efficiency |>
  summarise(.by = Model,
            ESS_per_hour = mean(ESS_per_hour),
            Time_total = mean(Time_total))

# What each fit was: two models are only comparable here if these match
caption <- efficiency |>
  summarise(.by = Model,
            label = sprintf("%s: %d chains, %g threads/chain, n = %s",
                            first(Model), n(), first(Threads),
                            format(first(N), big.mark = ","))) |>
  pull(label) |>
  paste(collapse = "\n")

efficiency |>
  ggplot(aes(x = ESS_per_hour, y = Time_total / 3600, colour = Model)) +
  # One point per chain, and the model's mean on top of them
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_point(data = efficiency_means, size = 5, shape = 18) +
  # Both axes log: families differ in cost per gradient by orders of magnitude
  # (the DDM's numerical quadrature is 55x, see cogmod_ddm_cost_issue.md), and
  # on a linear axis the cheap ones collapse onto the origin
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Effective sample size per hour of sampling (bulk ESS / h, log)",
    y = "Wall clock per chain, warmup included (hours, log)",
    title = "Computational cost",
    subtitle = "One point per chain, diamond is the model's mean. Bottom right is cheap and efficient.",
    caption = caption
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, colour = "grey40"))
```

```{r}
# Total compute, three ways, for a rough headline number:
# - Wall clock: the shards of a model run at the same time on the cluster, so
#   what one waited for is the longest chain (queueing, compilation and the
#   combine/loo step are not included).
# - Chains one after the other: the sum of the chain times, i.e. the same run
#   with no parallel chains but still multithreaded within each chain.
# - Single core: that sum times the threads per chain. This assumes within-
#   chain threading scales linearly, which is close to what was measured
#   (4 -> 8 threads halved the time per chain, server/AGENT.md 4.4.1), so read
#   it as an order of magnitude, not a measurement.
compute_time <- efficiency |>
  summarise(.by = Model,
            Chains = n(),
            Threads = first(Threads),
            Cores = n() * first(Threads),
            Wall = max(Time_total) / 3600,
            Serial = sum(Time_total) / 3600,
            SingleCore = sum(Time_total * Threads) / 3600) |>
  mutate(SingleCore_days = SingleCore / 24,
         SingleCore_years = SingleCore / (24 * 365.25))

compute_time |>
  gt::gt(rowname_col = "Model") |>
  gt::cols_label(
    Chains = "Chains",
    Threads = "Threads / chain",
    Cores = "Cores used",
    Wall = "Wall clock (h)",
    Serial = "Chains in sequence (h)",
    SingleCore = "Single core (h)",
    SingleCore_days = "Single core (days)",
    SingleCore_years = "Single core (years)"
  ) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(Wall, Serial, SingleCore, SingleCore_days), decimals = 0) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = SingleCore_years, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::tab_spanner(label = "Without parallelisation (estimated)",
                  columns = c(Serial, SingleCore, SingleCore_days, SingleCore_years)) |>
  gt::tab_source_note("Warmup + sampling only. Single core assumes linear scaling of within-chain threading.")
```

## Posterior Predictive Check


```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

plot_ppc <- function(models, observed = NULL, ndraws = 500, n_trials = 10000,
                     rt_range = c(0, 2.5), binwidth = 0.02, n_points = 512,
                     model_colors = c("#1E88E5", "#212121", "#FB8C00", "#6D4C41")) {

  if (is.null(names(models))) names(models) <- paste("Model", seq_along(models))

  # All models are checked against the same trials, passed in explicitly
  if (is.null(observed)) observed <- insight::get_data(models[[1]])

  # The predicted curve is the predictive RT distribution marginal over trials,
  # estimated by simulation. A random subset of trials estimates the same
  # distribution as all of them - each trial contributes ndraws simulated RTs
  # either way - so there is no reason to predict 320,000 trials x 50 draws
  # (16 million RTs per model, minutes per model) to draw a density curve that
  # 250,000 RTs already pin down. The histogram still uses every observed trial.
  pred_obs <- if (nrow(observed) > n_trials) {
    observed[sample.int(nrow(observed), n_trials), , drop = FALSE]
  } else {
    observed
  }

  # Defective densities: each response's curve is scaled by its own rate, so the
  # two areas sum to 1 and correct/error are directly comparable across models
  defective_density <- function(rt, response) {
    keep <- is.finite(rt) & is.finite(response)
    rt <- rt[keep]
    response <- response[keep]
    purrr::map_dfr(c(0, 1), function(r) {
      x <- rt[response == r]
      if (length(x) < 2) return(NULL)
      d <- density(x, from = rt_range[1], to = rt_range[2], n = n_points)
      data.frame(
        Response = factor(r, levels = c(0, 1)),
        x = d$x,
        y = d$y * (length(x) / length(rt)) * if (r == 0) 1 else -1
      )
    })
  }

  # Observed: histogram, put on the same defective-density scale
  obs_data <- observed |>
    mutate(bin = floor(RT / binwidth)) |>
    count(Error, bin, name = "n") |>
    mutate(
      x = (bin + 0.5) * binwidth,
      y = n / (nrow(observed) * binwidth) * if_else(Error == 0, 1, -1),
      Response = factor(Error, levels = c(0, 1))
    ) |>
    filter(x <= max(rt_range))

  # Predicted. brms::posterior_predict() calls the family's sampler once per
  # trial (thousands of calls of a few dozen draws each), and most of that is
  # fixed cost. cogmod's posterior_predict_<family>() methods take a vector of
  # observations, so the same draws come out of ~50 vectorised calls instead,
  # about 3x faster for the DDM - see ?posterior_predict_cogmod_ddm.
  predict_chunked <- function(m, newdata, ndraws, chunk = 50) {
    prep <- brms::prepare_predictions(m, newdata = newdata, ndraws = ndraws,
                                      allow_new_levels = TRUE)
    for (dp in names(prep$dpars)) prep$dpars[[dp]] <- brms::get_dpar(prep, dp)
    method <- get(paste0("posterior_predict_", m$family$name),
                  envir = asNamespace("cogmod"))
    chunks <- split(seq_len(prep$nobs), ceiling(seq_len(prep$nobs) / chunk))
    do.call(rbind, lapply(chunks, method, prep = prep))   # (draws * N) x 2
  }
  pred_data <- purrr::imap_dfr(models, function(m, nm) {
    pp <- predict_chunked(m, pred_obs, ndraws)
    rt   <- pp[, 1]
    resp <- pp[, 2]
    stopifnot(all(resp %in% c(0, 1)))
    defective_density(rt, resp) |> mutate(Model = nm)
  })
  pred_data$Model <- factor(pred_data$Model, levels = names(models))

  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_col(
      data = obs_data,
      aes(fill = Response),
      width = binwidth, alpha = 0.4
    ) +
    geom_line(
      data = pred_data,
      aes(color = Model, group = interaction(Model, Response)),
      linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.9
    ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("0" = "#43A047", "1" = "#F44336"),
      labels = c("0" = "Correct", "1" = "Error")
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = setNames(model_colors[seq_along(models)], names(models))) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = abs) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = rt_range) +
    labs(x = "RT", y = "Density", fill = "Observed", color = "Predicted") +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 0.6))) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

plot_ppc(
  models,
  observed = insight::get_data(models[[1]]),
  ndraws = 500
)
```

## Parameter Curves

### Compute Predictions

```{r}
# Display names for the parameters, in the order they are plotted. Names are
# the family's own ("mu", "ndt", ...), values are what goes in the panel
# titles. Several parameters mean different things from one family to the next
# - "mu" is a drift rate in the DDM and the log-mean of the correct response in
# the LNR, and "sigmabias" is the variability of the starting point in the DDM
# but its maximum (A) in the racing models - so the map is built per model.
param_labels <- function(gam) {
  lvls <- c("Error Rate" = "Error Rate",
            "Mean RT" = "Mean RT",
            "mu" = "mu",
            "nuone" = "Nu (Errors)",
            "driftone" = "Drift (Errors)",
            "sigmadrift" = "Drift Variability",
            "sigmazero" = "Sigma (Correct)",
            "sigmaone" = "Sigma (Errors)",
            "boundary" = "Boundary",
            "bias" = "Bias",
            "sigmabias" = "Bias Variability",
            "ndt" = "NDT",
            "sigmandt" = "NDT Variability")
  switch(
    insight::get_family(gam)$name,
    "cogmod_ddm" = {
      lvls["mu"] <- "Drift"
    },
    # sigmabias is only estimated in LNR-6, where it is the start-point range
    # of the race, as in the other racing families
    "cogmod_lnr" = {
      lvls[c("mu", "sigmazero", "sigmaone", "sigmabias")] <-
        c("Nu (Correct)", "Nu Variability (Correct)", "Nu Variability (Errors)",
          "Start Point Range")
    },
    # Both racing families: mu is the drift of the accumulator for correct
    # responses and driftone that of the other one, and sigmabias is the
    # start-point range A rather than a variability around a bias
    "cogmod_rdm" = {
      lvls[c("mu", "sigmabias")] <- c("Drift (Correct)", "Start Point Range")
    },
    "cogmod_lba2" = {
      lvls[c("mu", "sigmabias", "sigmazero", "sigmaone")] <-
        c("Drift (Correct)", "Start Point Range",
          "Drift SD (Correct)", "Drift SD (Errors)")
    }
  )
  lvls
}

# Rename the parameters and put them in canonical order. Parameter_Order keeps
# that order recoverable once the models are stacked together, where the factor
# levels of families that do not share their parameters get merged in whatever
# order the models happen to come in.
format_parameters <- function(pred, gam) {
  lvls <- param_labels(gam)
  found <- unique(as.character(pred$Parameter))
  # A parameter the map does not know about (a family added later) keeps its
  # own name and goes last, rather than silently becoming an NA panel
  unknown <- setdiff(found, names(lvls))
  if (length(unknown) > 0) lvls <- c(lvls, setNames(unknown, unknown))
  lvls <- lvls[names(lvls) %in% found]

  pred$Parameter_Order <- match(as.character(pred$Parameter), names(lvls))
  pred$Parameter <- factor(unname(lvls[as.character(pred$Parameter)]),
                           levels = unname(lvls))
  pred
}

# Predictions for each of the model's own parameters (mu and the auxiliaries,
# minus the outlier weight) over whatever grid is passed. The curves and the
# heatmaps below differ only in that grid, so they share this.
predict_parameters <- function(gam, datagrid) {
  params <- insight::find_auxiliary(gam)
  params <- c("mu", params[!params %in% c("poutlier")])
  purrr::map_dfr(params, function(p) {
    estimate_relation(gam, data = datagrid, predict = p) |>
      mutate(Parameter = p)
  })
}

# The illusion a fit was made on, as attached by load_fit()
model_illusion <- function(gam) {
  illusion <- attr(gam, "illusion")
  if (is.null(illusion)) stop("The model has no illusion recorded: load it with load_fit().")
  illusion
}

# The range of the space the curves and heatmaps are drawn over, per illusion
# and in raw units: strength signed, difference absolute (see normalize_units).
# An illusion not listed here is drawn over its full fitted range.
# TODO: custom ranges for the other illusions
plot_ranges <- list(
  MullerLyer = list(strength = c(-30, 30), difference = c(0.05, 0.45))
)

# Prediction grid of n_strength x n_difference points over that range,
# converted to the Z scale the models were fitted on
make_datagrid <- function(gam, n_strength = 31, n_difference = 5) {
  illusion <- model_illusion(gam)
  range <- plot_ranges[[illusion]]
  if (is.null(range)) {
    warning("No plot range set for ", illusion, ", using its full fitted range.")
    strength <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = n_strength)
    difference <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = n_difference)
  } else {
    strength <- normalize_units(seq(range$strength[1], range$strength[2], length.out = n_strength),
                                type = illusion, what = "Strength")
    difference <- normalize_units(seq(range$difference[1], range$difference[2], length.out = n_difference),
                                  type = illusion, what = "Difference")
  }
  insight::get_datagrid(gam, by = list(Illusion_DifferenceZ = difference,
                                       Illusion_StrengthZ = strength))
}

# Parameters against illusion strength, one curve per illusion difficulty
data_curves <- function(gam) {
  datagrid <- make_datagrid(gam, n_strength = 31, n_difference = 5)
  pred <- estimate_prediction(gam, data = datagrid, centrality = "mean",
                              # TODO: increase iterations
                              iterations = 500, keep_iterations = TRUE) |>
    mutate(Parameter = Component, Type = "GAM") |>
    select(-Component, -Row) |>
    mutate(Parameter = ifelse(Parameter == "response", "Error Rate", "Mean RT"))

  # Only keep iterations of correct responses to compute mean
  iters_rt <- data.frame(select(pred[pred$Parameter == "Mean RT", ], starts_with("iter_")))
  iters_rt[data.frame(select(pred[pred$Parameter == "Error Rate", ], starts_with("iter_"))) == 1] <- NA
  pred[pred$Parameter == "Mean RT", "Predicted"] <- rowMeans(iters_rt, na.rm = TRUE)
  # Remove mean RTs when only a few correct trials as it's noisy
  pred[pred$Parameter == "Mean RT", "Predicted"][pred[pred$Parameter == "Error Rate", "Predicted"] > 0.9] <- NA
  pred <- select(pred, -starts_with("iter_"))

  # Add the predictions for the parameters of the model itself
  pred <- rbind(pred, mutate(predict_parameters(gam, datagrid), Type = "GAM"))

  pred |>
    format_parameters(gam) |>
    # Restore the original scale of the illusion strength and difference
    restore_units(illusion = model_illusion(gam))
}

# Stack the models. Adding one to `models` in the loading chunk is all it takes
# for it to get its own column in every plot below.
preds_curves <- purrr::imap_dfr(models, \(m, name) mutate(data_curves(m), Model = name)) |>
  mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = names(models)))
```



### Visualize

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 10

# Column header
make_header <- function(label) {
  ggplot() +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = 0, y = 0,
      label = label,
      fontface = "bold",
      size = 5
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1)) +
    theme_void()
}

# Height of the column-header row, in units of one panel row. A figure that
# puts something alongside the grid has to skip the headers to line up with the
# panels, so this is a shared constant rather than a default buried in the
# function below.
parameter_grid_header <- 0.35

# Which parameter goes in which row of which column. The models do not share
# their parameters, so rows cannot be matched by name: each model's parameters
# are packed from the top in canonical order (which lines up the drift rates and
# the nus, both "mu"), and the non-decision time - the one parameter every
# family has - is anchored to the bottom row. Models with fewer parameters get
# NA in between, drawn as spacers, so the columns stay aligned however many
# parameters they have.
parameter_grid_rows <- function(data, anchor_bottom = c("NDT", "NDT Variability")) {
  data$Model <- droplevels(factor(data$Model))

  slots <- lapply(levels(data$Model), function(model) {
    d <- data[data$Model == model, ]
    params <- unique(as.character(d$Parameter[order(d$Parameter_Order)]))
    list(top = params[!params %in% anchor_bottom],
         bottom = params[params %in% anchor_bottom])
  })
  names(slots) <- levels(data$Model)
  n_top <- max(lengths(lapply(slots, `[[`, "top")))
  n_bottom <- max(lengths(lapply(slots, `[[`, "bottom")))

  lapply(slots, function(s) {
    c(s$top, rep(NA_character_, n_top - length(s$top)),
      rep(NA_character_, n_bottom - length(s$bottom)), s$bottom)
  })
}

# One column per model, one row per parameter, with panel(model, parameter)
# drawing each cell. The cells go into a single grid, filled column by column,
# rather than one sub-layout per model put side by side: patchwork only aligns
# panels within a layout, so separate columns let each one's rows drift with
# its own titles and legends.
plot_parameter_grid <- function(data, panel,
                                anchor_bottom = c("NDT", "NDT Variability"),
                                header_height = parameter_grid_header) {
  rows_by_model <- parameter_grid_rows(data, anchor_bottom)
  cells <- unlist(Map(function(model, rows) {
    c(list(make_header(model)),
      lapply(rows, function(p) if (is.na(p)) plot_spacer() else panel(model, p)))
  }, names(rows_by_model), rows_by_model), recursive = FALSE)

  wrap_plots(cells, ncol = length(rows_by_model), byrow = FALSE,
             heights = c(header_height, rep(1, length(rows_by_model[[1]]))))
}

# Prepare data
curves <- preds_curves |>
  filter(!Parameter %in% c("Error Rate", "Mean RT")) |>
  mutate(Illusion_Difference = factor(Illusion_Difference))

# Colour scale
curve_cols <- colorRampPalette(
  c("#FF5722", "#FFC107", "#8BC34A", "#4CAF50")
)(nlevels(curves$Illusion_Difference))

# Function for individual panels
make_curve <- function(model, parameter) {
  ggplot(
    filter(curves, Model == model, Parameter == parameter),
    aes(Illusion_Strength, Predicted, colour = Illusion_Difference)
  ) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.3) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = curve_cols) +
    labs(title = parameter, color = "Task Difficulty") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        hjust = 0.5,
        size = 11,
        margin = margin(b = 4)
      ),
      axis.title = element_blank()
    )
}

plot_parameter_grid(curves, make_curve) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 4, 4)
  )
```

## Parameter Heatmaps

### Compute Predictions

```{r}
# The same parameters as the curves, but over the full 2-D grid of illusion
# strength x illusion difference rather than five difficulty levels
data_heatmaps <- function(gam, n = 40) {
  datagrid <- make_datagrid(gam, n_strength = n, n_difference = n)
  predict_parameters(gam, datagrid) |>
    format_parameters(gam) |>
    restore_units(illusion = model_illusion(gam))
}

preds_heatmaps <- purrr::imap_dfr(models, \(m, name) mutate(data_heatmaps(m), Model = name)) |>
  mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = names(models)))
```

### Visualize

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 16.5

# Two ways of reading the values off the map: a colour bar per panel, or, as on
# an elevation map, the value written on a handful of the contour lines (which
# makes the colour bars redundant, so they are dropped)
heatmap_labels <- TRUE

# Function for individual panels
make_heatmap <- function(model, parameter) {
  d <- filter(preds_heatmaps, Model == model, Parameter == parameter)
  contours <- if (heatmap_labels) {
    list(
      # Few enough lines that the labels have room: 20 would overlap in panels
      # this short. Breaks strictly inside the range, as pretty() can overshoot.
      geomtextpath::geom_textcontour(
        # The label is given explicitly: the default rounds it, which writes
        # 0.4 on every NDT contour from 0.37 to 0.41. The sign is a true minus
        # (U+2212): geomtextpath 0.2.0 silently drops an ASCII hyphen, which
        # labels -3 as 3 and makes the colour scale look reversed.
        aes(z = Predicted,
            label = after_stat(sub("^-", "−", format(level, trim = TRUE, drop0trailing = TRUE)))),
        breaks = (\(b) b[b > min(d$Predicted) & b < max(d$Predicted)])(pretty(d$Predicted, n = 10)),
        size = 2.5, linecolour = "white", textcolour = "white", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.5,
        padding = grid::unit(0.5, "mm"), straight = TRUE
      ),
      guides(fill = "none")
    )
  } else {
    geom_contour(aes(z = Predicted), color = "white", alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.5, bins = 20)
  }

  ggplot(d, aes(x = Illusion_Strength, y = Illusion_Difference)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = Predicted)) +
    contours +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "white", linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed") +
    # The region of the space that might be psychometrically optimal
    annotate("rect", xmin = -30, xmax = 30, ymin = 0.1, ymax = 0.4,
             fill = NA, color = "red", linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "dotted") +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "turbo") +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(title = parameter, fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11, margin = margin(b = 4)),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      legend.key.width = grid::unit(0.25, "cm"),
      # A null height stretches the colour bar to the height of its panel, so
      # it can neither overflow into the panel below nor sit off-centre
      legend.key.height = grid::unit(1, "null"),
      legend.ticks = element_blank(),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 7)
    )
}

# Each parameter is on its own scale, so unlike the curves the fill guides
# cannot be collected: every panel keeps its own colour bar
heatmaps <- plot_parameter_grid(preds_heatmaps, make_heatmap) &
  theme(plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 4, 4))

# Every panel shares the same axes, so the titles are dropped from the panels
# (see make_heatmap) and written once around the whole grid, next to a strip of
# stimuli showing what each axis means. patchwork has no shared axis title: the
# titles and the images each get their own row/column of the layout (the
# plot.tag route needs two nested wrap_elements, which renders the grid blank in
# patchwork 1.3.2).
axis_title <- function(label, rot = 0) {
  wrap_elements(grid::textGrob(label, rot = rot, gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 13)))
}

# Muller-Lyer stimuli along each axis, rendered by
# illustrations/make_illustrations.py (re-run it if the stimulus bounds change).
# Both series are numbered low value to high, so they run in the direction of
# their axis: x left to right, y bottom to top, hence the reversal below.
illustrations_dir <- if (dir.exists("illustrations")) "illustrations" else "analysis/illustrations"

# Every stimulus is drawn at the same size on both axes. The images already
# share their pixel dimensions (make_illustrations.py crops them with one box),
# so an explicit height is all it takes -- with the width left out, rasterGrob
# takes it from the aspect ratio. Letting each raster fill its cell instead
# would size the y-axis ones by the column width and the x-axis ones by the row
# height, which come out different once patchwork has taken its margins.
stim_h <- 1.55  # height of every stimulus, in inches
stim_aspect <- local({
  d <- dim(png::readPNG(file.path(illustrations_dir, "mullerlyer_strength1.png")))
  d[2] / d[1]
})
illustration <- function(name, vjust = "centre") {
  wrap_elements(grid::rasterGrob(
    png::readPNG(file.path(illustrations_dir, paste0("mullerlyer_", name, ".png"))),
    # capped at the cell, so a figure too short for the strip shrinks it rather
    # than clipping it
    height = grid::unit.pmin(grid::unit(stim_h, "in"), grid::unit(1, "npc")),
    y = grid::unit(c(top = 1, centre = 0.5, bottom = 0)[[vjust]], "npc"),
    just = c("centre", vjust),
    interpolate = TRUE
  ))
}

# The outer two mark the ends of the y axis, so they sit flush with the top and
# the bottom of the panel block rather than floating in the middle of their cell
y_strip <- wrap_plots(
  Map(illustration, paste0("difference", 3:1), c("top", "centre", "bottom")),
  ncol = 1
)
x_strip <- wrap_plots(lapply(paste0("strength", 1:3), illustration), nrow = 1)

# The y-axis column starts at the first panel, not at the column headers. The
# row count is recomputed rather than carried out of plot_parameter_grid(): a
# stale value here silently collapses the heights to an even split, which puts
# the strip in the bottom half of the grid.
grid_rows <- length(parameter_grid_rows(preds_heatmaps)[[1]])
below_header <- function(p) {
  wrap_plots(plot_spacer(), p, ncol = 1, heights = c(parameter_grid_header, grid_rows))
}

# The strip and title rows/columns are sized in inches and the grid takes the
# rest ("null"). Relative sizes would be read against the panels rather than the
# cells, which leaves the strips adrift from the grid they annotate.
wrap_plots(
  below_header(axis_title("Task Difficulty", rot = 90)), below_header(y_strip), heatmaps,
  plot_spacer(), plot_spacer(), x_strip,
  plot_spacer(), plot_spacer(), axis_title("Illusion Strength"),
  ncol = 3,
  widths = grid::unit(c(0.3, stim_h * stim_aspect + 0.2, 1), c("in", "in", "null")),
  heights = grid::unit(c(1, stim_h + 0.2, 0.3), c("null", "in", "in"))
)
```


## Best Model

A bespoke visualization of the best model.

```{r}
layout <- matrix(c(
  rep(1, 5), rep(2, 5),  # Column 1 (Left): 5 units for the main outcomes
  rep(3, 2),             # Column 2 (Right): 2 units each for remaining 5
  rep(4, 2),
  rep(5, 2),
  rep(6, 2),
  rep(7, 2)
), ncol = 2, byrow = FALSE)

preds_curves |> 
  filter(Model == "LNR") |>
  mutate(Illusion_Difference = as.factor(Illusion_Difference)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = Illusion_Strength, y = Predicted)) +
  # geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = CI_low, ymax = CI_high, group = Illusion_Difference), alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_line(aes(color = Illusion_Difference, group = interaction(Type, Illusion_Difference), linetype = Type),
            linewidth = 1.5) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = colorRampPalette(c("#FF5722", "#FFC107", "#8BC34A", "#4CAF50"))(length(unique(preds_curves$Illusion_Difference)))
    ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("GAM" = "solid", "LM" = "dashed")) +
  # facet_wrap(~Parameter, scales = "free_y") +
  ggh4x::facet_manual(vars(Parameter), design = layout, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_minimal()
```
